rationale_overall: This week's pool was heavy on noise that needed discarding before any signal could be read: North Korea's ICBM parade and a nuclear-warship espionage arrest are geopolitical but not investable; SpaceX itself, GalaxEye, Pakistan's HS-1 satellite and AiMOGA Robotics are private or foreign-listed with no liquid US line; 'Rocket Doctor AI', Rio Tinto and Fortescue 'could rocket X%' headlines are keyword false-matches (medtech penny stock and Australian miners, not space vehicles); IsoEnergy/Toro Energy and Uranium Royalty are thin Canadian uranium names without a clear US liquidity floor. Net of that filtering, the genuine signal was incremental confirmation of existing theses rather than a new catalyst: Rocket Lab's JAXA contracts and StriX launch (rockets_spacecraft) are real buildup evidence but represent continued execution of an already-known trend, not an inflection strong enough to displace a current holding; Amazon/Army SMR progress and Lyon County nuclear siting reinforce the existing SMR position rather than argue for a swap; and the AI data-center deal flow (Google India, BlackRock/Nvidia $40B, Intel Crescent Island, Meta/Arm) reinforces NVDA/GOOGL exposure without naming a new must-own vehicle. No current holding (AAPL, GOOGL, NVDA, SMR) showed a thesis breach or peak-euphoria signal this week, so no remove is warranted, and per the pairing rule that means no add either. Watchlist shape is unchanged: AI (NVDA, GOOGL, AAPL) and near-term nuclear (SMR) alongside the SPY/AGG/IAU anchors.
